Right now, our health care system isn’t working. We need to lower the cost of prescription drugs, hold big corporations accountable for price-gouging, ensure everyone can access primary care, and never make families choose between getting the care they need or paying their bills. Every day I am fighting to protect and improve our most vital programs, including Medicare and Medicaid. Soon after I got to Congress, I introduced the Affordable Pricing for Taxpayer-Funded Prescription Drugs Act. This bill would lower prescription drug prices by preventing pharmaceutical companies from price-gouging Americans on drugs that are developed with taxpayer money. We need to address rural inequities in healthcare. COVID-19 has devastated the financial stability of rural practices, disrupted small economies, and only exacerbated the healthcare workforce shortage. We know that rural and senior populations often encounter barriers to healthcare that limit their ability to obtain the care they need, and I’m focused on fighting for representation and funding for our rural communities. Housing is an issue that is top of mind for people who live across coastal and Southwest Oregon. In our coastal communities, short-stay rentals make housing problems even worse. The inflated cost of housing across Oregon’s Fourth District, along with a vacancy rate well below the national average, is hurting working families and makes it more difficult for employers to recruit workers. I support expanding affordable and workforce housing. I support tax policies that create more opportunities for first-time home ownership, and I oppose tax policies that subsidize the already-wealthy, including hedge funds that buy up property and contribute to inflated real estate prices.

The brave men and women who serve our country are owed our gratitude and support. Our veterans need access to physical and mental healthcare, expanded housing options, and good-paying jobs to help transition back to civilian life. I’m committed to working closely with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to ensure we are doing everything we can to increase access to services and benefits for all veterans. Our country made a promise to our veterans, and I have every intention of seeing it through.

This includes increasing teacher pay and workforce retention, reducing class sizes, increasing our investments in public schools, supporting special needs programs, ensuring our schools are safe, and much more. As a first-generation college student, I understand the value of investing in higher education and ensuring it is affordable. I want to make sure everyone has a seat at the table, and I also understand the challenges with having student loan debt That’s why I support efforts to reduce student loan debt, double the Pell Grant, end supplemental taxation of Pell Grants, and fight against predatory loan practices that target vulnerable students. Oregon’s Fourth Congressional District is home to two top research universities, the University of Oregon and Oregon State University, as well as 5 community colleges . These institutions are critical to our communities, providing students from diverse backgrounds with access to quality education and training. They are centers of innovation and job training, contributing significantly to the local economy and job market.

I’m proud to serve on the House Natural Resources Committee, which considers legislation related to our public lands and waters. I strongly support managing our natural resources to protect our environment and special places, while also providing economic opportunities to our rural communities. We can ensure that future generations can enjoy Oregon’s world class landscapes while keeping rural jobs in the woods and on fishing boats. My bill, the Southwestern Oregon Watershed and Salmon Protection Act, would permanently protect Southwestern Oregon rivers, clean drinking water, wild salmon habitats, and outdoor recreation from mining pollution. I’m doing everything I can to get this bill signed into law.

The Fourth District hosts numerous modes of transportation and infrastructure that are vital to our communities and local economies, including ports, railroads, airports, interstate and state highways, rural roads, public transit, hiking and biking trails, and more. Oregon’s rural and coastal communities face particular transportation and infrastructure challenges. As the federal government works to implement the historic infrastructure bill that President Biden and congressional Democrats passed in 2021 – the “Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act” – I am committed to ensuring that our rural and coastal communities are not left behind. I am also using my position on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee to fight for better wages, hours, and working conditions for transportation and infrastructure workers in Oregon and across the country. These workers have our backs when we drive, fly, and ride; when we need infrastructure built or repaired; and more. I’m fighting in Congress to ensure we have their backs too.

HOYLE VOTES FOR CONTINUING RESOLUTION WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representative Val Hoyle (OR-04) released the following statement after voting for a continuing resolution to keep the federal government funded through December 11th. “As costs continue to rise, it's the American people that are paying the price for the political circus in Washington. Instead of voting on a full budget, House Republicans have decided to kick the can down the road and vote on a short-term continuing resolution through December 11th. While this bill isn’t perfect, we cannot afford another government shutdown that will disrupt vital services the American people rely on, deny federal employees their incomes and further damage the American economy. These are real problems that deserve real solutions. While I am here ready to work, my Republican colleagues are leaving working families behind. That's shameful.” ###   Print   Email   Share   Tweet Previous Article Next Article
